categories.name: HID & USB Emulation
categories.description: Core P4wnP1 keyboard, mouse, and composite USB device capabilities

tools.name: P4wnP1 Core Service
tools.description: Main P4wnP1 ALOA daemon: HID keyboard/mouse emulation, DuckyScript engine, USB gadget management, web UI on port 8000

tools.name: DuckyScript Sample Library
tools.description: Extended library of DuckyScript payloads for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Includes helpers for PowerShell, bash injection, and mouse automation.

tools.name: USB Mass Storage Image Tools
tools.description: Tools for creating and managing USB mass storage images: genisoimage (ISO creation), mkdosfs (FAT formatting), losetup utilities

categories.name: Network Services
categories.description: DHCP, DNS, NAT, proxying, and network infrastructure tools

tools.name: dnsmasq (DHCP + DNS Server)
tools.description: Lightweight DHCP and DNS server. Powers P4wnP1's USB network interface. Supports DNS spoofing, custom leases, and DNS sinkholing.

tools.name: hostapd (WiFi AP)
tools.description: IEEE 802.11 AP and authentication server. Creates WiFi access points when a compatible USB WiFi adapter is connected. Required for Evil Twin attacks.

tools.name: iodine (DNS Tunneling)
tools.description: Tunnels IPv4 data through DNS queries. Enables network connectivity through firewalls that only allow DNS traffic.

tools.name: iw + wireless-tools
tools.description: Linux wireless configuration tools: iw (nl80211), iwconfig, iwlist, iwpriv. Required for USB WiFi adapter management and monitor mode.

tools.name: OpenVPN
tools.description: Full-featured SSL/TLS VPN. Create encrypted tunnels from the Pi Zero back to attacker infrastructure or home network.

tools.name: WireGuard VPN
tools.description: Modern, fast, and lightweight VPN. Lower CPU overhead than OpenVPN — ideal for the Pi Zero's limited resources. Useful for persistent C2 tunnels.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.description: Command-line network packet analyzer. Captures and displays network traffic in real time. Essential for network analysis and debugging.

tools.name: tshark (Wireshark CLI)
tools.description: Terminal version of Wireshark for deep packet inspection and protocol analysis. Supports hundreds of dissectors and filtering expressions.

tools.name: nginx (Web Server / Reverse Proxy)
tools.description: High-performance web server and reverse proxy. Host phishing pages, serve payloads, or proxy HTTPS traffic for MITM attacks.

tools.name: SSLsplit (HTTPS Interception)
tools.description: Transparent SSL/TLS interception proxy. Decrypts HTTPS traffic for inspection by acting as a MITM. Requires CA cert installation on targets.

tools.name: Responder (LLMNR/NBNS Poisoning)
tools.description: LLMNR, NBT-NS, and MDNS poisoner for Windows credential capture. Responds to name resolution requests and captures NTLMv1/v2 hashes.

tools.name: nftables / iptables
tools.description: Linux firewall and NAT framework. Configure traffic routing, NAT for internet sharing, port forwarding, and packet filtering rules.

tools.name: autossh (Persistent SSH Tunnels)
tools.description: Automatically restarts SSH sessions and tunnels when they drop. Useful for maintaining reliable reverse shells or persistent port forwards.

categories.name: Security Research
categories.description: Authorized penetration testing and vulnerability assessment tools

tools.name: nmap (Network Scanner)
tools.description: Industry-standard network discovery and security auditing tool. Port scanning, service version detection, OS fingerprinting, and NSE scripting.

tools.name: masscan (Fast Port Scanner)
tools.description: Internet-scale port scanner. Faster than nmap for large IP ranges. Useful for quickly identifying open services across a network.

tools.name: nikto (Web Vulnerability Scanner)
tools.description: Open-source web server scanner. Tests for dangerous files, outdated server software, and common vulnerabilities including XSS, SQLi indicators.

tools.name: sqlmap (SQL Injection Testing)
tools.description: Automated SQL injection detection and exploitation tool. Tests for SQLi vulnerabilities and can enumerate databases, extract data, or execute commands.

tools.name: Hydra (Brute Force Tool)
tools.description: Multi-protocol login cracker. Tests SSH, FTP, HTTP, SMB, and 50+ other protocols against wordlists. For authorized credential testing.

tools.name: John the Ripper (Password Cracker)
tools.description: Fast password cracker supporting hundreds of hash types. Includes wordlist attacks, rules-based mutation, and incremental modes.

tools.name: hashcat (GPU/CPU Hash Cracker)
tools.description: Advanced password recovery using CPU. Supports MD5, SHA-1, bcrypt, WPA2, NTLM, and thousands of other algorithms.

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.description: Comprehensive penetration testing framework with exploit modules, post-exploitation tools, and payload generation. Requires ~1.5GB disk space.

tools.name: Impacket (Windows Protocol Tools)
tools.description: Python library for Windows protocols: SMB relay, Kerberoasting, Pass-the-Hash, NTLM capture, Active Directory enumeration.
tools.uninstall_cmd: pip3 uninstall -y impacket 2>/dev/null; apt-get remove -y python3-impacket 2>/dev/null; true

tools.name: netcat / ncat
tools.description: The TCP/IP Swiss Army knife. Create listeners for reverse shells, port forward, banner grab, and transfer files over TCP/UDP.

tools.name: socat (Socket Cat)
tools.description: Enhanced netcat with SSL support, UNIX sockets, PTY shells, and complex relay/proxy setups. Better than netcat for encrypted reverse shells.

tools.name: ExploitDB / searchsploit
tools.description: Local copy of Exploit-DB for searching known exploits by software name, CVE, or platform. Offline access to thousands of PoC exploits.

tools.name: enum4linux (SMB/LDAP Enumeration)
tools.description: Enumerates Windows and Samba systems: users, groups, shares, policies, and domain info. Useful for Active Directory reconnaissance.

tools.name: SecLists / Wordlists
tools.description: Collection of security wordlists: passwords, usernames, fuzzing strings, web paths, DNS subdomains. Essential for brute-force and fuzzing attacks.

categories.name: WiFi & Wireless
categories.description: Wireless network analysis and testing tools (requires USB WiFi adapter)

tools.name: aircrack-ng Suite
tools.description: Complete WiFi security auditing suite: airmon-ng (monitor mode), airodump-ng (capture), aireplay-ng (injection/deauth), aircrack-ng (WPA cracking). Requires USB adapter with monitor mode support.

tools.name: bettercap (Network Attack Framework)
tools.description: Swiss-army knife for network attacks: ARP spoofing, MITM, WiFi probe sniffing, BLE scanning, and web-based control interface.

tools.name: Kismet (Wireless IDS / Sniffer)
tools.description: Wireless network detector, sniffer, and IDS for 802.11, Bluetooth, and Zigbee. Passive monitoring and channel hopping for network mapping.

tools.name: mdk4 (WiFi Stress Testing)
tools.description: WiFi stress testing tool for authorized network testing: deauthentication, authentication flooding, and beacon flooding for resilience testing.

tools.name: hcxdumptool (WPA Handshake Capture)
tools.description: Captures WPA/WPA2 handshakes and PMKID without deauthentication. Used for offline WPA password cracking with hashcat.

tools.name: wpa_supplicant (WiFi Client)
tools.description: WPA/WPA2/WPA3 client daemon. Connects the Pi Zero to WiFi networks as a client when USB WiFi adapter is attached.

categories.name: GPIO & Sensors
categories.description: Hardware interface libraries for GPIO pins, I2C, SPI, and sensor modules

tools.name: RPi.GPIO + gpiozero
tools.description: Python GPIO control libraries for the Pi Zero's 40-pin header. gpiozero provides a high-level API; RPi.GPIO offers low-level pin access.

tools.name: pigpio (Advanced GPIO)
tools.description: Advanced GPIO library with microsecond-level timing, hardware PWM, and daemon mode for remote control. Better timing precision than RPi.GPIO.

tools.name: i2c-tools
tools.description: I2C bus exploration tools: i2cdetect (scan for devices), i2cget/i2cset (read/write registers). Essential for connecting sensors via I2C.

tools.name: SPI Tools + python3-spidev
tools.description: SPI interface tools and Python library for communicating with SPI sensors, displays, and devices like the MCP3008 ADC.

tools.name: Adafruit / Circuit Python Sensor Libraries
tools.description: Python libraries for common sensors: DHT22 temperature/humidity, BMP280 pressure, MPU6050 IMU, DS18B20 temperature, and many others.

tools.name: gpiozero Extras (Motion, Distance, LEDs)
tools.description: Python support for PIR motion sensors, HC-SR04 ultrasonic distance sensors, servo motors, RGB LEDs, and H-bridge motor drivers via gpiozero.

categories.name: IoT Protocols
categories.description: MQTT, Zigbee, Z-Wave, LoRa, and other IoT communication protocols

tools.name: Mosquitto (MQTT Broker + Client)
tools.description: Lightweight MQTT message broker and client tools. Enables IoT device communication, sensor data routing, and smart home automation via MQTT.

tools.name: Node-RED (Visual IoT Automation)
tools.description: Flow-based programming environment for wiring together IoT devices and APIs. Drag-and-drop editor for automation workflows. Accessible via browser.
tools.uninstall_cmd: systemctl disable --now nodered 2>/dev/null; npm uninstall -g node-red 2>/dev/null; rm -f /etc/systemd/system/nodered.service; systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null; true

tools.name: zigbee2mqtt (Zigbee Bridge)
tools.description: Bridges Zigbee devices to MQTT. Supports 3000+ Zigbee devices from Philips Hue, IKEA, Xiaomi, etc. Requires USB Zigbee coordinator.

tools.name: CoAP Tools (Constrained IoT Protocol)
tools.description: Python-aiocoap for implementing CoAP clients and servers. CoAP is used by constrained IoT devices with limited bandwidth.

tools.name: ChirpStack (LoRaWAN Gateway)
tools.description: Open-source LoRaWAN network server stack. Bridges LoRa devices to cloud platforms. Requires USB LoRa concentrator hardware.

tools.name: Modbus Tools (Industrial Protocol)
tools.description: Python pymodbus library for Modbus RTU and TCP communication with industrial PLCs and SCADA equipment. For authorized ICS security research.

categories.name: Media Services
categories.description: Audio streaming, video serving, game emulation, and multimedia tools

tools.name: MPD + ncmpc (Music Player Daemon)
tools.description: Background music player with client-server architecture. Stream audio to connected devices via HTTP, DLNA, or USB audio output.

tools.name: ffmpeg (Multimedia Processor)
tools.description: Complete multimedia framework for transcoding video/audio, streaming, recording, and format conversion. Supports RTMP, HLS, RTSP output.

tools.name: Icecast2 (Internet Radio Server)
tools.description: Open-source audio streaming server. Broadcasts audio streams over HTTP. Compatible with VLC, Winamp, and most media players.

tools.name: RetroArch (Game Emulator)
tools.description: Multi-system emulator frontend supporting NES, SNES, GBA, Genesis, and arcade cores. Play retro games over network or on connected display.

tools.name: Jellyfin (Media Server)
tools.description: Open-source personal media server. Streams movies, TV shows, and music to any device. Self-hosted alternative to Plex.

categories.name: Development Tools
categories.description: Programming languages, version control, containers, and development servers

tools.name: Python 3 Development Stack
tools.description: Python 3 with pip, venv, development headers, and common libraries. The base for most Pi Zero scripting and automation tasks.

tools.name: Node.js + npm
tools.description: JavaScript runtime for backend development and IoT tooling. Required for Node-RED, zigbee2mqtt, and many other tools.

tools.name: git
tools.description: Distributed version control system. Clone repositories, manage code, and pull tool updates directly on the Pi Zero.

tools.name: Docker (Container Runtime)
tools.description: Containerization platform for running isolated applications. Supports ARM/arm32v6 images. Enables portable app deployment on the Pi Zero.

tools.name: code-server (VS Code in Browser)
tools.description: Run Visual Studio Code in the browser. Code directly on the Pi Zero from any device. Access at http://172.16.0.1:8443

tools.name: SQLite3 (Embedded Database)
tools.description: Lightweight embedded database engine. Ideal for Pi Zero's limited resources. Used by many applications for local data storage.

tools.name: Go (Golang) Runtime
tools.description: Go programming language toolchain for ARM. Compile Go programs natively on the Pi Zero. Required for building P4wnP1 from source on-device.

tools.name: Gitea (Self-Hosted Git Server)
tools.description: Lightweight self-hosted Git service with web UI. Host private repositories on the Pi Zero. Accessible from PC or Android via browser.
tools.uninstall_cmd: systemctl disable --now gitea 2>/dev/null; rm -f /usr/local/bin/gitea /etc/systemd/system/gitea.service; systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null; true

categories.name: Monitoring & Logging
categories.description: System monitoring, metrics collection, and centralized logging

tools.name: Prometheus + Node Exporter
tools.description: Time-series metrics collection and alerting system. Node exporter collects CPU, memory, disk, and network metrics from the Pi Zero.

tools.name: Grafana (Metrics Dashboard)
tools.description: Visual analytics and monitoring dashboards. Connect to Prometheus or InfluxDB and create real-time visualizations accessible from browser.

tools.name: InfluxDB (Time-Series Database)
tools.description: High-performance time-series database for sensor readings and metrics. Pairs with Grafana for sensor data visualization.

tools.name: logwatch + rsyslog
tools.description: Centralized system logging with rsyslog and daily log analysis with logwatch. Forward logs from remote systems to the Pi Zero.

tools.name: netdata (Real-Time System Monitor)
tools.description: Real-time performance monitoring with built-in web dashboard. Low overhead monitor for CPU, memory, network, and disk. Accessible at port 19999.

categories.name: SDR & Radio
categories.description: Software-defined radio for RF monitoring, ADS-B, and spectrum analysis

tools.name: RTL-SDR Tools
tools.description: Software-defined radio drivers and tools for RTL2832U-based USB dongles. Enables spectrum scanning, signal capture, FM radio, and ADS-B aircraft tracking.

tools.name: dump1090 (ADS-B Aircraft Tracker)
tools.description: Decodes ADS-B aircraft transponder signals from RTL-SDR. Real-time aircraft position tracking with web-based map display.

tools.name: gqrx (SDR Receiver)
tools.description: Software-defined radio receiver application with spectrum analyzer. Requires display or X11 forwarding. Supports RTL-SDR, HackRF, and other SDR hardware.

tools.name: GNU Radio
tools.description: Toolkit for building software-defined radio systems. Create custom signal processing pipelines using Python or visual flowgraph editor.

categories.name: Home Automation
categories.description: Smart home platforms, automation hubs, and building control systems

tools.name: Home Assistant
tools.description: Open-source home automation platform integrating 3000+ smart home devices and services. Web UI at port 8123. Requires 1GB+ free disk space.
tools.uninstall_cmd: systemctl disable --now homeassistant 2>/dev/null; pip3 uninstall -y homeassistant 2>/dev/null; rm -f /etc/systemd/system/homeassistant.service; systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null; true

tools.name: openHAB
tools.description: Vendor-neutral open-source home automation platform. Integrates with KNX, Z-Wave, Zigbee, MQTT, and 400+ other bindings.

tools.name: Matter / Thread Border Router
tools.description: Python chip-tool for Matter protocol and OpenThread border router daemon. Connects Thread mesh networks and controls Matter-based smart home devices.

categories.name: Infrastructure & Networking
categories.description: VPN mesh networks, lightweight Kubernetes, distributed systems

tools.name: k3s (Lightweight Kubernetes)
tools.description: Production-grade Kubernetes for resource-constrained devices. Run containerized workloads on the Pi Zero as part of a cluster.

tools.name: Tailscale (Zero-Config Mesh VPN)
tools.description: WireGuard-based mesh VPN that works through NAT and firewalls. Creates a private network between all your devices without port forwarding.

tools.name: avahi (mDNS / Bonjour)
tools.description: mDNS/DNS-SD implementation for zero-configuration networking. Makes the Pi Zero discoverable as 'p4wnp1.local' without manual DNS configuration.

tools.name: OpenSSH Server
tools.description: SSH server for remote shell access to the Pi Zero. Manage the device remotely over USB network or WiFi without physical access.
